title: Hidden Star-Convexity in Policy Optimization for Gain-Scheduled LQR: Extended Version
summary: We study policy optimization for gain-scheduled linear quadratic regulation, where one schedule of gains, interpolated through fixed weighting functions, is optimized against a family of plants. The resulting cost can develop spurious local minima, and existing convergence certificates are either local or severely conservative. We establish an exact identity: when the gradient of the cost is evaluated with the minimizer's closed-loop covariances, the scheduled cost is star-convex about the minimizer. The identity holds on the entire feasible set, for any parametrization of the schedule.…
